title: US markets and the Federal Reserve Board closed — Washington's Birthday (the closure the January minutes class is structurally unable to collide with)
source: NEWS: TWO INDEPENDENT PRIMARIES AGREE AND A STATUTE REPRODUCES BOTH, all three checked by this session on 2026-09-09. (1) nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, fetched direct (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes) -- the page states 'All NYSE markets observe U.S. holidays as listed below for 2026, 2027, and 2028' and its cells, parsed one by one, read 'Washington's Birthday | Monday, February 16 | Monday, February 15 | Monday, February 21' against the year headers 2026 / 2027 / 2028, with no early-close footnote anywhere in February. (2) federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/k8.htm, fetched direct (HTTP 200, 82,205 bytes, stamp 'Last Update: July 8, 2026') -- its own holiday table gives 'Washington's Birthday | February 16 | February 15 | February 21 | February 19 | February 18' across the 2026-2030 columns, so the BOARD is closed the same day, unasterisked. (3) Reproduced by statute and weekday arithmetic independent of both: 5 U.S.C. 6103 fixes Washington's Birthday on the THIRD MONDAY in February, and the third Monday of February 2028 is 2028-02-21 (2028-02-01 is a Tuesday, computed from 2028-01-01 being a Saturday). Filed estimate on the same taxonomy grounds the sibling closure entries presidents-day-market-closure-2027-02-15, good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26, memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31 and labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07 all documented, not on date doubt: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange's own holiday calendar, and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt -- the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED by the fomc-minutes-2028-02-16 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-09), at D+5 from that release, inside the +/-5 corridor -- which was otherwise COMPLETELY EMPTY across all 837 tracked events and proposals, this being the calendar's furthest-out researched print. LOAD-BEARING AS A MEASURING STICK, not as a trade. fomc-minutes-2027-12-29.md established that FOMC-minutes displacement from D+21 tracks distance from the BOARD OF GOVERNORS' own closure rather than from a holiday week: |gap| <= 1 runs 4 displaced of 5, |gap| >= 2 runs 0 of 14. The proposing lane's own structural result is that a January-class release can NEVER enter the dangerous band, because this closure is always a Monday and a D+21 release from a last-Wednesday-of-January decision is always a Wednesday -- so the gap is quantised to exactly {+2, -5} and was one of those two values in all 18 historical cases. 2028-02-16 sits at -5. That is why the January sub-class is 18-for-18 at D+21 while November is 6-for-14 on the exception list: structure, not luck. NOTHING TRADEABLE IS CLAIMED -- a full closure trades nothing by definition, symbols is empty, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is calendar-keyed. Two second-order facts a later lane may want: the closure compresses the week of 2028-02-21 to four sessions, and it sits one session after the 2028-02-18 monthly expiration proposed in the same PR. Proposed as an estimate; estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
